<!-- SECTION: 11 Why Source Cat Apparel from China -->
<section id="why-source-china">
  <h2><span class="section-num">11</span> Why Source Cat Apparel from China</h2>
  <p>If you've only ever bought cat clothes from a domestic distributor, the math of a <strong>China pet clothing supplier</strong> can feel too good to be true — until you see the supply chain behind it. China's pet-apparel clusters (Guangdong, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu lead) bundle fabric mills, trim houses, and sewing lines within a short drive of each other. That density is why a <strong>pet apparel factory China</strong> can move from a sketch to a finished sample in days, not months, and why small brands get the same production discipline once reserved for big-box orders.</p>
  <p>Three advantages matter most for a boutique or Amazon seller. <strong>Cost:</strong> because labour, fabric, and finishing sit in one ecosystem, ex-factory pricing runs roughly <strong>$12–$22 per piece</strong> — versus $29–$75 retail for comparable "designer" cat apparel in Western markets. <strong>Original-design capacity:</strong> our in-house studio develops cohesive looks you won't find cloned across ten competitor feeds, so your shelf stays distinctive. <strong>Flexible small runs:</strong> the same line that fills a container for a chain will also run a 200-piece trial for a startup, because flexible <strong>cat apparel wholesale China</strong> production is now the norm, not the exception.</p>
  <p>To make that concrete: the <a href="../products/cat-grey-velvet-waistcoat.html">grey velvet waistcoat (low MOQ)</a> leaves our line at roughly $12–$16 ex-factory and retails around $34–$45 in boutiques — a margin that funds marketing and repeat buys. The <a href="../products/cat-white-victorian-gown.html">white Victorian gown (MOQ 200)</a> sits higher in both cost and retail, but its "heirloom portrait" appeal drives the kind of gift-season volume that pays back a small first order quickly. Sourcing from China isn't about chasing the cheapest stitch; it's about buying original design at a price that lets your business breathe.</p>
  <p>Curious how we manage the supply side for you? Our <a href="../services.html#sourcing">China sourcing agent</a> service handles supplier selection end to end — the topic of section 15 below.</p>
</section>


<!-- SECTION: 12 Custom & Private Label Cat Clothing -->
<section id="custom-private-label">
  <h2><span class="section-num">12</span> Custom &amp; Private Label Cat Clothing</h2>
  <p>Loving a design is one thing; owning it as your brand is another. That's where OEM comes in. With Youna as your <strong>OEM pet clothes manufacturer</strong>, our original silhouettes become your label: we apply your woven logo tags, match your brand colourway, and print or emboss your packaging so the piece arrives as unmistakably yours. Nothing about the garment references Youna unless you want it to — the cat sees the same comfort, your customer sees your brand.</p>
  <p>This is what <strong>private label pet clothing</strong> is built for: a small brand can launch a "designer" cat line without hiring a pattern maker or auditioning ten factories. You pick the hero pieces from the collection above, tell us your trim and palette, and we return a sample wearing your identity. Because the underlying designs are original and owned by us, you get the look of a luxury house with none of the trademark risk that sinks resellers of borrowed logos.</p>
  <p>For true differentiation, <strong>custom cat clothes OEM</strong> goes a step further: we adjust necklines, add a collar, swap a fabric, or develop an entirely new colourway for your range. When the goal is to design custom cat outfits for my brand rather than re-label a template, our OEM studio develops fresh silhouettes to your brief. The <a href="../products/cat-floral-garden-dress.html">floral garden dress (custom OEM)</a> and the <a href="../products/cat-white-victorian-collar-dress.html">Victorian collar dress (private label)</a> are two frequent starting points for brands wanting a signature piece. And remember the callout in our sidebar — <strong>Low MOQ from 200 pcs</strong> — means a private-label trial doesn't require a warehouse-sized commitment.</p>
  <p>Ready to put your name on original design? Explore our <a href="../custom-oem-private-label.html">OEM &amp; private label pet apparel</a> program, or talk to us about <a href="../services.html#branding">custom branding</a> and <a href="../services.html#branding">private label service</a> options for the cat line.</p>
</section>


<!-- SECTION: 13 MOQ, Pricing & Lead Time for Cat Apparel -->
<section id="moq-pricing-lead-time">
  <h2><span class="section-num">13</span> MOQ, Pricing &amp; Lead Time for Cat Apparel</h2>
  <p>Buying wholesale should feel like reading a spec sheet, not decoding a riddle. Here are the working numbers for our cat apparel line — the same figures a <strong>low MOQ pet clothing manufacturer</strong> partner would quote, laid out plainly so you can plan cash flow and launch dates.</p>
  <div class="table-responsive">
    <table class="article-table">
      <thead>
        <tr><th>Term</th><th>Standard</th><th>Notes</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>MOQ</td><td>200 pcs / style</td><td>Mix colours within a style to hit the minimum.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Ex-factory price</td><td>$12–$22 / pc</td><td>Varies by fabric weight and trim complexity.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Sample lead time</td><td>5–7 days</td><td>Pre-production sample for your sign-off.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Bulk lead time</td><td>12–20 days</td><td>After sample approval; rush slots on request.</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Shipping</td><td>By air or sea</td><td>Air ~7–12 days; sea ~25–35 days to major ports.</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
  <p>Those bands answer the questions B2B buyers type most: <strong>cat apparel MOQ China</strong> buyers typically find 200/style here versus 500–1,000 at many factories; <strong>cat clothes bulk order pricing</strong> stays in the $12–$22 ex-factory window even at scale, because our cluster sourcing keeps fabric costs down. A 200-piece trial of the <a href="../products/cat-grey-velvet-waistcoat.html">grey velvet waistcoat (low MOQ)</a> at ~$14 average lands near $2,800 in goods — a realistic first order for a Shopify store testing the category.</p>
  <p>Two planning notes. First, sample time and bulk time are sequential, so budget about 3–4 weeks door-to-door by air from sample request to stock. Second, the $12–$22 figure is ex-factory; your landed cost adds freight, duties, and fulfillment, which our team estimates per order. For the full picture on getting goods from a <strong>cat clothing manufacturer China</strong> to your warehouse, see section 15.</p>
</section>


<!-- SECTION: 14 How a China Sourcing Agent Simplifies Cat Apparel Import -->
<section id="sourcing-agent">
  <h2><span class="section-num">14</span> How a China Sourcing Agent Simplifies Cat Apparel Import</h2>
  <p>Sourcing cat clothes from China sounds straightforward until the first container arrives with the wrong colour and no recourse. A <strong>cat clothes sourcing agent</strong> exists to close that gap — and Youna has done it for hundreds of businesses since 2016. Rather than you negotiating blind with a factory you've never met, we run the import as a managed process.</p>
  <p>It starts with <strong>supplier screening</strong>: we shortlist audited pet-apparel factories against your spec, not a marketplace listing. Next is the <strong>factory audit</strong> — on-site checks of capacity, labour, and quality systems so you're not trusting a polished brochure. Once production runs, our <strong>quality control</strong> team inspects against the approved sample at key stages, catching a mis-cut size run before it ships instead of after. Finally, we handle <strong>logistics</strong>: consolidation, freight booking, and customs paperwork, so a <strong>China sourcing agent pet apparel</strong> engagement ends with cartons at your door, not a panic at the port.</p>
  <p>This is also the practical answer to <strong>how to import cat clothes from China</strong> without hiring a Guangzhou office. Our <a href="../services.html#sourcing">China sourcing agent</a> service covers screening through shipping, while <a href="../services.html#branding">custom branding</a> and <a href="../services.html#branding">private label service</a> fold labelling and packaging into the same workflow. The result is fewer surprises: you approve one sample, we protect that standard through bulk, and you receive what you signed off on. For a small brand, that reliability is worth more than the few cents a factory-direct "deal" might save — and loses the moment something goes wrong.</p>
  <p>Want the playbook step by step? The next section turns this process into an actionable launch plan.</p>
</section>

<div class="pdp-faq">
  <div class="pdp-faq-item">
    <h4>What are designer cat clothes?</h4>
    <p>Designer cat clothes are original, brand-owned garments made for cats using premium fabrics and considered tailoring — not licensed knockoffs of human luxury labels. They prioritize a cat's comfort, safe fastenings, and a distinct aesthetic you won't see repeated on every feed.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="pdp-faq-item">
    <h4>What fabrics are best for cat clothes?</h4>
    <p>The best fabrics for cat clothes are soft, breathable, and low-irritation: cotton, jersey, velvet, lightweight denim, satin blends, and lace used as trim or overlay. Avoid stiff, heat-trapping synthetics that rub sensitive skin.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="pdp-faq-item">
    <h4>Are clothes safe for cats?</h4>
    <p>Yes — when made from soft, breathable fabric with easy-release fastenings and worn for short, supervised sessions. Always check for rubbing, overheating, or stress, and remove the garment if your cat seems distressed.</p>
  </div>
</div>
